results.title: ‘Jim Crow must go’: the artists and everyday heroes who fought injustice – in pictures - The Guardian
results.content: # ‘Jim Crow must go’: the artists and everyday heroes who fought injustice – in pictures. at the Nasher Museum of Art at Duke University highlights the activism of everyday people who have confronted injustice. New York’s mayor, Zohran Mamdani, quoting the Bronx rapper KRS-One’s song Turn the Volume Up during his election-day victory speech inspired the name of the exhibit. Featuring work by artists such as Kara Walker, Carrie Mae Weems and the Guerrilla Girls, the show examines how protests and collective action can create and inspire social change. opens on 27 August and runs through 11 July 2027. results.title: ’We are united‘: King Charles III and President Macron attend private preview of London's Bayeux Tapestry exhibition - The Art Newspaper
results.content: # ’We are united‘: King Charles III and President Macron attend private preview of London's Bayeux Tapestry exhibition. ## Likely commissioned in France but made in England, the tapestry could have been called ‘the Canterbury Embroidery’ joked the King in a speech. The King said in a speech that the exhibition in London is an example of how “we are united” and a “reminder of what our countries can do if they join forces”. “Crucial in the timing of the loan this time is the closure of the Bayeux Tapestry Museum [in Normandy], which shut in September 2025, so that it can be extended and refurbished,” he said. 1 September 2026#### A bonanza of Bayeux Tapestry books to accompany the blockbuster British Museum exhibition. #### A bonanza of Bayeux Tapestry books to accompany the blockbuster British Museum exhibition.

results.title: Young adults with experience of having parents in prison to curate exhibition at London’s Southbank Centre - The Art Newspaper
results.content: # Young adults with experience of having parents in prison to curate exhibition at London’s Southbank Centre. ## Rock, Paper, Scissors will bring together more than 200 works by people in criminal justice settings. Young adults who have had a parent in prison will curate an exhibition at London’s Southbank Centre this autumn, sharing their experiences in the process. *Rock, Paper, Scissors*, the latest edition of the annual Koestler Arts exhibition, will bring together more than 200 works selected from over 7,500 entries to the 2026 Koestler Awards, which recognise art made by people in prisons, secure hospitals, young offender institutions and other criminal justice settings. This year, the works have been chosen by five members of the Parental Imprisonment Collective (PIC), a group of 18 to 35-year-olds from across the UK who experienced parental imprisonment. The artists will remain anonymous to visitors to, under an HMPPS policy introduced in 2023 that prevents Koestler Arts from displaying prisoners’ first names alongside their work.

results.title: ‘We don't think it should be controversial to talk about these subjects’: Bonniers Konsthall opens exhibition on art as antifascist resistance ahead of Swedish election - The Art Newspaper
results.content: # ‘We don't think it should be controversial to talk about these subjects’: Bonniers Konsthall opens exhibition on art as antifascist resistance ahead of Swedish election. ## The group show ‘The Defeated: The Aesthetics of Resistance 2026’, which opened in Stockholm this week, is inspired by the antifascist, postwar literature of German-Swedish writer Peter Weiss. A new exhibition in Sweden explores antifascist art and the role of culture and art in navigating today's fraught politics, before the country goes to the polls later this month. Bonniers Konsthall, a contemporary art institution in Stockholm, presents the timely show *The Defeated: The Aesthetics of Resistance 2026* (until 8 November) featuring works by 19 international artists. This exhibition borrows its title from two books by the Swedish-German artist, filmmaker and playwright Peter Weiss (1916–82): *The Defeated (De besegrade),* written in Swedish and published by the Bonniers publishing house in 1948, and *The Aesthetics of Resistance*, written in German and published in three volumes between 1975 and 1981.

results.title: Metropolitan Museum and designer John Galliano cancel planned Costume Institute exhibition amid backlash - The Art Newspaper
results.content: The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York and the British fashion designer John Galliano have called off an exhibition honouring Galliano that was planned for next spring, following a wave of opposition in light of the designer’s history of antisemitic statements. In a statement on Monday (31 August), Max Hollein, the director and chief executive of the Met, said: “Following thoughtful discussions with John Galliano, we have together decided not to proceed with the exhibition.”. Champions of his work over the years have included Anna Wintour, the former editor-in-chief of *Vogue*, a trustee of the Met and the chair of the Met Gala since 1999, and Andrew Bolton, the curator in charge of the Met’s Costume Institute and lead organiser of the planned exhibition, *John Galliano: Horizons*. According to *The New York Times*, the decision to cancel the exhibition came just hours before planned meetings on Monday of select members of the museum’s board and the full Met leadership and board of trustees to discuss the exhibition’s future and matters related to the Costume Institute.
